description:
pkix-lint/src/lib.rs:823:

    #[allow(unused_variables)]
    fn set_parameter(&mut self, id: &str, value: &str) -> Result<(), ParameterError>;

The doc comment describes what to return on success and on
UnknownParameter / InvalidValue. It does NOT state whether the lint's
internal state is unchanged when Err is returned. For lints with
multiple internal fields that get derived from the parameter value
(e.g., a future lint that parses 'min-rsa-bits' into both `min_bits:
usize` and `derived_strength_class: enum`), partial-update on parse
failure is silently possible.

Compare to LintRunner::apply_parameter_overrides (lib.rs:1180-1183):

    /// Errors short-circuit on the first failure — overrides applied
    /// before the failing one remain mutated on the lints. Callers
    /// that need atomic application should resolve and validate
    /// overrides against the catalog before installing the lints in a
    /// runner.

This documents the BATCH atomicity (non-atomic), already filed
in PKIX-hy2e.6. But the trait method itself doesn't say whether
*one* call is atomic.

Currently the only shipped lint with parameters
(Rfc5280MaxSerialLengthLint) has one parameter and one internal
field (max_octets). The single-field write is naturally atomic.
But the trait contract does not say so.

# What the caller cannot rely on

A caller writing a third-party lint with multiple parameters that
correlate — say, 'min-rsa-bits' and 'min-rsa-bits-after-2030' — has
no contract that says 'either both update or neither does'. Their
mental model is whatever the implementor decided.

# Suggested fix

Document the per-call atomicity contract in the rustdoc, EITHER:

  - 'set_parameter is atomic: on Err, the lint's state is identical
    to before the call. Implementors MUST validate inputs before
    mutating fields.'

  OR

  - 'set_parameter is not atomic. Implementors MAY leave the lint
    in a partially-updated state on Err. Callers needing atomicity
    should restore state via a known-good config replay.'

The 'MUST validate inputs before mutating fields' contract is the
better default — it's also what Rfc5280MaxSerialLengthLint already
does (parse first, mutate after).

# Cheapest fix

Add to set_parameter rustdoc: '# Atomicity: On Err, the lint's
internal state is unchanged. Implementors MUST parse and validate
the value before mutating any state.' (Then every implementor has a
documented contract to satisfy.)
title: API contract: Lint::set_parameter does not document atomicity on Err
